name: Tower Semiconductor Ltd.
sector: Semiconductors / Specialty analog foundry (silicon photonics, RF, SiGe)
moat_justification: A differentiated specialty foundry, not a scale leader: Tower leads in silicon photonics for AI data-center optical interconnect and holds deep, hard-to-replicate process know-how across SiPho, SiGe BiCMOS, RF SOI and CMOS image sensors, where customer designs are qualified onto specific process recipes and switching means re-qualification. Contracted SiPho demand ($1.3B of customer contracts for 2027 revenue per management) and $290M of customer prepayments evidence real stickiness. Capped at moderate: Tower is sub-scale versus TSMC/GlobalFoundries, has no leading-edge logic position, historically earned only thin foundry margins through the cycle (FY2024-25 gross profitability fell back after the 2023 one-off year), and its growth is now concentrated in one hot end-market (AI optical) whose demand and pricing it does not control, funded by a capex program ($920M plan in the 20-F) that consumes all of its operating cash flow.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x1.0 ordinary shares per ADS (Tower Semiconductor Form 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025 (SEC filing, CIK 928876), Item 9: 'Our ordinary shares are listed and traded on the NASDAQ Stock Market ... and on the TASE under the symbol TSEM' — the security registered under Section 12 is the ordinary shares themselves, listed directly on Nasdaq; there is no depositary/ADS program.) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
one_liner: Real specialty-foundry franchise riding the AI silicon-photonics wave, moat 5/10 — but conservative owner's earnings are negative on the normalized base (-$0.19/share) and in the latest FY (-$0.76/share) because capex absorbs all operating cash flow, so it cannot clear 15% at $209.16 on an OE DCF at any scenario; Tier F until the capacity build converts to positive OE.
moat_for: Leading silicon photonics foundry position for AI data-center optical interconnect — SiPho at a $680M annualized run rate in Q2 2026, guided to cross $1B in Q4 2026
Deep specialty process know-how (SiPho, SiGe BiCMOS, RF SOI, BCD power, CMOS image sensors) — customer designs qualified onto Tower recipes are slow and expensive to move
Contracted demand visibility: ~$1.3B of SiPho customer contracts for 2027 and ~$290M of customer prepayments received
Multi-fab footprint across Israel, the US and Japan (with Japanese government/METI support for the 300mm expansion) — a scarce diversified-supply asset
Net-cash balance sheet (engine net debt -$73,851,000) funds the expansion without forced dilution
moat_against: Sub-scale specialty player: no leading-edge logic, and larger foundries (TSMC, GlobalFoundries, Intel) are all pushing into silicon photonics
Capex intensity consumes the business: capex $444,425,000 in FY2025 exceeded operating cash flow; the $920M expansion plan plus a further Japan build-out keep OE negative while capacity is built

Growth concentration in AI optical interconnect — a single end-market and a narrow set of transceiver customers; an AI capex slowdown or a co-packaged-optics architecture shift hits the core growth leg
Thin through-cycle pricing power: FY2025 revenue grew only 9.05% and net income was $220,470,000 on $1,566,104,000 of revenue despite the SiPho ramp already starting
Capacity execution risk: the Japan dual-track expansion must be built, qualified and filled at high utilization for the raised 2028 target model ($3.6B revenue) to hold
